- The client adds items to the basket. _(fig. calls 1-3)_
- The admin lists all items from the catalog to get the IDs of the items. _(fig. calls 4-5)_
- The admin deletes an item from the catalog. _(fig. calls 6-7)_

**Description of the bugs:**

**1. Absence of cascading delete:** each basket item contains the ID of the corresponding catalog item, resembling a foreign key. However, when the catalog item is deleted (fig. call 7), this action is not propagated to the basket, leaving a reference that is no longer valid.

During checkout (or even when viewing the cart), the web app's [`FetchBasketItemsAsync`](https://github.com/dotnet/eShop/blob/1b2698cd83ed5c9e00a2fa954f2586c87022c431/src/WebApp/Services/BasketState.cs#L117) receives data from querying the basket (fig. calls 9-10, where the returned item IDs contain the deleted item ID) that is inconsistent with the data obtained from querying the catalog (fig. calls 11-12, where the returned items do not contain the deleted item).

The web app's [`FetchBasketItemsAsync`](https://github.com/dotnet/eShop/blob/1b2698cd83ed5c9e00a2fa954f2586c87022c431/src/WebApp/Services/BasketState.cs#L117)  expects that every basket item is present in the returned catalog items, and during iteration, a `key not found` error occurs, causing the web app to crash and remain unavailable.

**2. Concurrent operations:** even if cascading effects are implemented, bugs may still occur if the admin deletes the item from the catalog concurrently with the client adding the item to the basket.
